presenters.name: Isla Brodie
presenters.persona: Lead anchor, early 40s, from Edinburgh. Calm, precise, quietly funny. Keeps the show moving and reins in the pundits with a dry one-liner when they get carried away. Never gives her own opinion on football.

presenters.name: Fraser Lennox
presenters.persona: Co-anchor and resident old-timer, 61. Came through the Hearts youth ranks in the 1980s but never made the first team, and has watched from the Wheatfield Stand ever since. Old school: hates VAR with a passion, distrusts xG and 'laptop football', rates grit, wingers who beat their man, and centre-halves who head it. Nostalgic about the Jim Jefferies era and the 1998 Scottish Cup. Gruff but warm, prone to 'in my day'. Reads the news straight; his opinions come out in discussion.
leanings: always backs the academy players and anyone who came through the ranks
sceptical of the manager's in-game changes and late substitutions
rates a centre-half who heads it over one who plays it out from the back

presenters.name: Ross Dunbar
presenters.persona: Transfer Centre reporter, 26. Tactics nerd: talks about pressing triggers, inverted full-backs, xG and progressive carries. Obsessed with Fantasy Premier League and the SPFL fantasy game, always picking 'differentials'. Loves a rumour, gets excited quickly, winds Fraser up on purpose. Supports VAR.
leanings: trusts the numbers over reputation, when there are numbers to go on
gets excited by every new signing and is quick to call a rumour a done deal
backs the manager's tactical ideas, especially the press and the inverted full-backs

presenters.name: Kirsty Reid
presenters.persona: Match analyst, 34, former Hearts Women midfielder. Straight-talking and evidence-led, explains the game clearly without jargon. Champions the women's team, and is the voice of reason between Fraser and Ross.
leanings: evidence first: won't judge a player on one game
cautious about rushing players back from injury
always makes the case for Hearts Women getting more attention

presenters.name: Gregor Moffat
presenters.persona: Pitchside reporter, late 50s, from Kirkcaldy. Forty years on the road and has been to every ground in Scotland. Only appears live from the ground on matchdays, from the press seats among the home support. Breathless when the ball hits the net ('oh, he's caught that sweetly!'), always finds a word for the weather and the pies, and always hands back with 'back to you in the studio'.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Good afternoon, and welcome to Hearts News 24. It is Saturday, thirty-first of October 2026, and all eyes are on the national stadium as the Edinburgh derby approaches. Let us take a look at the headlines.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Wouter Vrancken has described the upcoming Premier Sports Cup semi-final against Hibernian as an all-or-nothing encounter. The Hearts manager admits he does not yet know his full available squad, while Hibs boss Marink Reedijk expects tactical surprises at Hampden tomorrow.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Twelve pundits have been having their say on tomorrow's big derby clash at Hampden. The Jambos have been handed major backing from the tipsters, while Marink Reedijk faces a huge opportunity to turn his side's fortunes around.

graphic.title: 12 pundits predict Hearts vs Hibs: Jambos handed major Hampden backing but Reedijk has huge endearment chance

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Heart of Midlothian have confirmed that left-back Harry Milne suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury in training last week. Head coach Wouter Vrancken announced that the defender's season is now over.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: BBC Sport reports that Martin Boyle is set to make his return for Hibernian in tomorrow's semi-final match. Hibs head into the fixture looking for a spark despite sitting second-bottom of the Premiership table.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Later today, Ross and Fraser go head to head with their derby predictions, and we will hear from the supporters in the Fan Zone.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Let us take a deeper look at the build-up now. Ross is standing by at the touchscreen to break down the key details.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Back to our top story, and there is no let up in the build-up to tomorrow's League Cup semi-final against Hibernian at Hampden. Ross, we have got all the latest team news and the tactical picture for this huge derby.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: That is right Isla. Wouter Vrancken says he does not yet know who will be fully available for Sunday, and Josh McPake's injury still needs to be assessed before kick-off. Meanwhile, Marink Reedijk says we can expect some surprises.

graphic.text: It's a totally different game. New manager, new style, new competition.
graphic.author: Wouter Vrancken

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: The Daily Record reports that ticket demand has been huge, with Hearts selling out their initial allocation and pushing total attendance past twenty-three thousand, alongside over eighteen thousand Hibs fans.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: The numbers back up our tactical control, Isla. Vrancken wants to replicate past success here and called it an all-or-nothing game.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Hibs come into this sitting second-bottom of the Premiership with only two points from their last eight games, and they have not kept a league clean sheet this season.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Reedijk's side have struggled for goals, scoring just once in their recent draw at Saint Mirren, though Martin Boyle does return for them with five derby goals historically under his belt.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: And looking at the officials for tomorrow, David Dickinson is the referee, assisted by David McGeachie and Douglas Ross, with Calum Scott fourth official, Andrew Dallas on VAR, and Nick Walsh as AVAR.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Now let us check the wider picture in the Match Centre with Kirsty, before we look ahead to tomorrow.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Hearts drew two-two at home to Rangers in the Scottish Premiership three days ago, with Cláudio Braga and Cameron Miller on the scoresheet.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Harry Milne is one short of fifty appearances for Hearts ahead of this derby, while Elton Kabangu is one goal away from ten for the club, and Blair Spittal needs two more.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Hearts sit third in the Scottish Premiership on twenty points from eleven games, four points behind Rangers in second and three ahead of Dundee in fourth.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Hearts face Hibernian in the League Cup tomorrow with kick-off at three pm.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Staying with the numbers, let us examine our opponents closely to see how Hibernian are shaping up.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Hibernian come into the derby sitting twelfth in the Premiership on eight points, looking to turn around a recent run that includes three defeats and a draw against St Mirren.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Head to head, in 343 league and cup meetings Hearts have won 153, drawn 102 and lost 88. At home it's 79 wins, 52 draws and 36 defeats. The last time Hearts beat Hibernian was in September twenty twenty-six, three-one away. The biggest win was eight-three, in September nineteen thirty-five.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Hibernian lined up in a four-two-three-one shape in their last outing, with Sallinger in goal behind a back four of Passlack, Kerr, Ivezic, and Mayor.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Hearts lined up in a four-two-three-one formation in their last match featuring Reus in goal, alongside Altena, Fagan-Walcott, McCart, and Mato, with Mendy and Magnússon holding the midfield.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Let us return to the main semi-final build-up now with Ross, who has been looking at some interesting player connections.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: More now on the build-up to tomorrow's League Cup semi-final at Hampden, and Ross, Jamie McCart has been talking about his friendship with Hibs defender Jason Kerr.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: That is right Isla, and the Daily Record reports that despite crossing the Edinburgh divide, their bond remains strong from their time winning the double together at St Johnstone in twenty twenty-one.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: McCart has certainly seen a shift in his own fortunes this season, hasn't he?

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: He really has, jumping from under seven hundred minutes last term under Derek McInnes to over sixteen hundred minutes already under Wouter Vrancken, and his physical metrics prove he is vital for our defensive press tomorrow.

graphic.text: I’ve reiterated that to the boys about my memories in 2021. It's such a good feeling
graphic.author: Jamie McCart

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: And he has had to deal with quite a few defensive partner changes alongside him.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Indeed, but with Malachi Fagan-Walcott back from injury, McCart feels the current setup and Vrancken's coaching style suit him down to the ground as they chase a first League Cup win since nineteen sixty-two.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: That tactical picture brings us straight into the debate. Fraser is ready with his match predictions.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Ross, you keep talking about your laptop analytics and pressing triggers, but this is the Edinburgh derby at Hampden. Our front four speed can dismantle Hibs if we manage the fatigue properly, exactly as I said yesterday.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Fraser, it is not just a hunch, it is about Vrancken's attacking metrics and tactical control proving decisive. My prediction record of two right from three speaks for itself compared to your one from three.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Your metrics do not win local derbies on the Hampden turf, grit and physical presence do. Jamie McCart needs to win his headers against their front line, and we need proper fighters on the pitch, not spreadsheet analysts.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Jamie McCart physical numbers prove he is vital for the derby press, Fraser. The analytics firmly justify us being favourites, and I am sticking to my comfortable three-nil win for Hearts.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Three nil is living in a dream world when Martin Boyle is back to threaten us. I am predicting a narrow two-one victory for Hearts over Hibernian because our momentum will carry us through.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: We'll take a short break now. Stay with us.

lines.speaker: vo-lily
lines.text: Fancy a day out in Gorgie that doesn't involve a forty-minute queue for a pie?

lines.speaker: vo-lily
lines.text: Come and meet the pigs, the goats and the rest of the gang at Gorgie Farm, a proper community farm right here in the city.

lines.text: Gorgie Farm. The only kids in Gorgie who are happy on a Monday.

graphic.tagline: A proper community farm in the middle of the city

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Ninety minutes of shouting at the referee builds up an appetite.

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Whether it's a fish supper after the final whistle or a chippy on a cold Tuesday night, Gorgie Fish Bar has got you covered.

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Salt and sauce? Of course. This is Edinburgh.

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Gorgie Fish Bar. Battered, never beaten.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Welcome back to Hearts News 24.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Let's return to the defensive situation at Hearts, Kirsty, and the latest on Eduardo Ageu.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: We were expecting him back next week to help ease our defensive selection issues.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Has something changed with that timeline?

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Unfortunately yes, as a muscle injury setback now keeps him out for weeks, making rushing defensive returns even more risky.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: And how does that impact the squad given the current injury list?

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: With Harry Milne ruled out for the season and others like Craig Halkett and Stuart Findlay sidelined, our options at the back are severely stretched.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Let us head over to the Transfer Centre now for the latest news from Ross.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Welcome to the Transfer Centre. The transfer window is currently closed and reopens in sixty-two days.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: That is the Transfer Centre for now. Let us turn back the clock with Fraser for On This Day.

segments.title: 31st October
segments.strap: On this day in Hearts history - stats from London Hearts

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Time for On This Day, our look back through the Hearts history books, and it's the 31st of October.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Former Hearts players born on this day include Ricardo Fuller and Kevin Twaddle.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: And on this day in twenty twenty, Hearts beat Hibernian two-one in the Scottish Cup semi-final, at Hampden. The goals came from Craig Wighton and Liam Boyce.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: On this date in two thousand and seven, Hearts beat Celtic two-nil in the League Cup quarter-final.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: And in twenty fifteen, Hearts beat Partick Thistle four-nil.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: And across the city, on this day in nineteen eighty-nine, Hibs lost one-nil to Liegeois (Liege) in the UEFA Cup. Not that anyone here is counting.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Back to the present day and tomorrow's threat. Isla is ready to examine the return of Martin Boyle.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Staying with the build-up to tomorrow's semi-final at Hampden, let's look at the threat posed by Martin Boyle's return for Hibs, Fraser.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: And how do you view Wouter Vrancken's approach to this all-or-nothing fixture compared to their previous meeting this season?

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Vrancken is right to say the first game doesn't matter anymore. Marink Reedijk's side have struggled for clean sheets and goals lately, whereas our momentum and over twenty-three thousand fans making the trip will secure the win.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Let us trace our path to this stage now, looking at how the team has progressed in the competition so far.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Another story we have been following today is Hearts and their progress in the League Cup.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Fraser, Wouter Vrancken has been speaking ahead of tomorrow afternoon's semi-final against Hibernian at Hampden. How are you assessing his approach?

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: As the Daily Record reports, Vrancken has been keen to keep the squad grounded despite his past trophy wins in Belgium giving him the right mentality for Hampden.

graphic.text: It's always the form of the day so you have to prepare well as an individual also
graphic.author: Wouter Vrancken

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: He knows all about pressure from the Conference League group stage and his time abroad, and over twenty-three thousand Hearts supporters will be right behind them.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: He is certainly playing down past successes and focusing entirely on tomorrow.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Time for a quick break. Don't go anywhere.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Welcome back to Hearts News 24.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: The fans are absolutely buzzing for Hampden tomorrow with massive ticket demand and high expectations for the derby.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Let us head over to the fan zone now and see what the supporters are saying on Jambos Kickback ahead of tomorrow.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Well Isla, the ticket thread is flooded with fans sorting out spares and making travel plans, and you can just feel the anticipation building.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: There is also plenty of discussion about the women side after their five-goal win against Boroughmuir at Meadowbank last night.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Brilliant result for the ladies, absolutely terrific. And over on the Hearts Standard preview show, the lads were right into the tactical side of things against Hibs.

lines.text: Though some supporters on the forum are still debating whether our front four can keep up the intensity without picking up more fatigue issues.

lines.text: Rubbish, our supporters will create an unbeatable atmosphere at Hampden and the pace we have got will blow them away if we get it right.
